handled_verified.note: Thirty types, every one pinned. The six `atx_hN_marker` and two `setext_hN_underline` types are how a heading's LEVEL is read — from the marker's own name, never from the marker's text, so a document that indents its heading markers differently still nests correctly. `atx_heading`/`setext_heading` are the two containers and they are handled TOGETHER because their text lives in different places: an ATX heading's text is its `inline` child, a setext heading's is the first line of its paragraph, and the analyzer branches on the container type rather than falling through from one to the other. That branch is not cosmetic — see the MD-D7 entry in the design decisions, where the wrong branch published a heading name containing a newline. `fenced_code_block` + `info_string` + `language` are the code-fence triple: the block is the site, the info string names the language, and the `language` child is preferred over the info string's own text because a fence can carry a title after the language. `pipe_table` + `pipe_table_header` + `pipe_table_cell` are the table triple, and the pair `minus_metadata` / `plus_metadata` is deliberately NOT a triple — see the plus_metadata gap entry. `link_destination` is read in BOTH grammars' shapes (an inline link's own child, and a reference definition's destination) and `link_label` carries the reference in the full form while `link_text` carries it in the collapsed and shortcut forms, so the three reference-link types plus those two are one contract, not five. `image` is read only for its REFERENCE form; an inline-form image's destination is its `link_destination` child and is already handled. `document` is the walk root.

internal_silent.note: Thirty-nine types that correctly emit nothing, each with a measured reason rather than a shrug. INLINE PRESENTATION (17 types): `emphasis`/`emphasis_delimiter`/`strong_emphasis`/`strikethrough`/`code_span`/`code_span_delimiter`/`hard_line_break`/`latex_block`/`latex_span_delimiter`/`backslash_escape`/`entity_reference`/`numeric_character_reference`/`link_text`'s siblings — formatting is not a graph fact. The load-bearing member of this group is `code_span`: a link inside one is excluded STRUCTURALLY, because the inline grammar gives a code span only ANONYMOUS children and the walker descends NAMED children only, so no `link_destination` is reachable beneath it. That is a property a reader can check, and it is what F9-PROBE-MD6 pins — if a future grammar gave `code_span` a named destination child, the probe fails and the exclusion has to become an explicit guard. A link inside `strong_emphasis` IS published, because those are named nodes with named children, and that is also correct. `latex_block` and `latex_span_delimiter` are the math forms; they carry no destination and no identity. LIST STRUCTURE (9 types, measured 6,264 `list_item` sites over 372 files): a list is a container, its items are containers, and its markers are presentation. What the lane DOES publish from inside a list is every link in its inline content, which the M12 contract probe pins ('link inside list item uses edge'). TASK MARKERS (2 types, 17 checked sites in 1 file): a checkbox is state, not a name; the doc declares them as noise. BLOCK CONTAINERS (6 types): `paragraph` and `section` are the grammar's structural wrappers — `section` in particular is a pure nesting artifact with no content of its own; `block_quote`/`block_quote_marker`/`block_continuation` likewise, and the links inside a quote ARE published (contract probe: 'link inside blockquote uses edge', 49 quote sites over 25 files). `thematic_break` (212 sites over 200 files) is `---`/`***`/___ and is worth naming for a specific reason: it is visually identical to a setext H2 underline, so a reader who assumed the marker was a break would mis-describe every setext heading in the lane. FENCE FURNITURE (2 types, 4,076 `code_fence_content` sites over 607 files): the fence's body text and its ``` delimiters are not facts; the language and the site are. TABLE FURNITURE (5 types, 224 `pipe_table_row` sites over 14 files): the analyzer reads the table's HEADER row and stops. A body cell is DATA — the same ruling toml's spec records for a value, and it is why a 224-row corpus of table bodies produces no symbols and no edges. RAW HTML (2 types, 579 `html_block` sites over 291 files — the largest silent class in the lane): the block grammar models a raw HTML block as an opaque region, and the companion inline grammar's `html_tag` covers inline raw HTML. Neither is a link destination. The corpus-errors artifact already names the one place this costs real recovery (`<details>` indented inside a numbered-list item, an ERROR at each list-item boundary), and that is a GRAMMAR limitation recorded against the grammar, not an analyzer gap. ZERO-SITE TYPES, named so the count is on the record rather than implied: `entity_reference` and `numeric_character_reference` are 0 over 738 files, which is why the character-reference ruling below is declared rather than measured. ERROR AND MISSING ARE THE ENGINE'S, NOT THE ANALYZER'S, and that boundary is the whole reason they are here rather than in handled_verified: `engine.ts` walks the parsed tree and pushes a `ParseError` for every `node.type === "ERROR" || node.isMissing` (the one condition, the one diagnostic, anchored to the offending node's own 1-based span), while `real-markdown-analyzer.ts` names NEITHER literal — measured, 0 occurrences in its source. So a markdown parse error is reported by the shared engine path every language uses, and the lane's own error contract is the four NAMED grammar limits in markdown-corpus-errors.json, not a recovery walk: 12 error nodes over 4 of 738 corpus files, all four named, 0 unexpected, 0 crashes. This is the same split the html spec records for the same two types, reached independently on a second grammar — ERROR reported, MISSING silent — and the useful part is that two lanes agree on it by measurement rather than by copying.  **`plus_metadata` is in this list for a reason worth reading twice: it is not the analyzer's choice, it is the GRAMMAR's.** The type is DECLARED in the pinned block grammar's node-type list, which is why the union census counts it among the 72 named types, but the grammar never INSTANTIATES it. Measured: the bare Pandoc `+++` form parses to a `paragraph`; the MyST `<!--[metadata]>` + `+++` form parses to an `html_block`; and across all 5,501 markdown files in every pinned corpus, 18 carry MyST title-block metadata and the grammar produces ZERO `plus_metadata` nodes for any of them. The gap entry that used to carry this asked for the `+++` form to be 'decided by measurement against a real MyST corpus when one is pinned' — that measurement has now been made, and it answers the question by removing it: a branch on the front-matter path keyed to this node type would be DEAD CODE, because the node never arrives. The only way to read a `+++` title block is to parse the paragraph's text, which is exactly what this lane's zero-regex, AST-derived-everything rule forbids. If a future grammar instantiates the node, `validation/m14/grammar-pins.json` goes red on `typeSetDigest` or `fieldSetDigest` and this entry is where the obligation is written down — that is the mechanism, and it already exists.

decisions.question: Should a reference link with NO matching `link_reference_definition` publish a `uses` edge to its bare label? RULED: no. CommonMark is explicit — 'If a link reference definition has not been defined for the link label, then it is not a link', and the construct renders as literal text.
decisions.measured: The alternative was implemented and MEASURED before being rejected: publishing the undefined case produced 171 edges across 34 of 738 corpus files, and sampling them showed the class dominated by bare bracketed citation markers (`NOTICE.md: document -> 1`, six times in one file). Those are fabricated endpoints and an R10 target-spelling violation, because `1` is not a name this lane spells its symbols with.
decisions.consequence: An undefined reference is INVISIBLE rather than flagged, so a reader cannot distinguish 'this document has a broken reference' from 'this document never had one'. That is a real limitation and it is a decision. The two rejected alternatives were publishing 171 fabrications, or inventing a suppression heuristic — and a heuristic with no evidence behind it is what this repository refuses most loudly.
decisions.pinned_by: F9-PROBE-MD1b, whose FORBID half also asserts the ORACLE refuses it, so the day the oracle starts deriving it the probe fails as COLLUSION rather than the lane quietly agreeing with itself.

decisions.question: Is a heading's published NAME its source text or its rendered text? RULED: its source text, with exactly two corrections that are grammar facts rather than style — the ATX closing run is removed, and an empty heading publishes ABSENCE.
decisions.measured: The rendered-text alternative has NO corpus evidence: `entity_reference` and `numeric_character_reference` are 0 over 738 files, and a 99-line fixture corpus is not a basis for a contract. So the source-text spelling stands, the two corrections stand on the pinned grammar's own shape, and the wider question is recorded here as UNDECIDED rather than answered by assertion.
decisions.consequence: Two headings that RENDER identically but differ in markup publish two symbols (`## **Setup**` and `## Setup`), and a formatting-only edit changes a symbol's identity. Stated rather than hidden. The corrections are load-bearing on their own: without the closing-run removal a document that closes its headings and one that does not produce two symbols for the same section, and without the absence rule a document of empty headings publishes a `contains` chain named `#` -> `##` -> `###`, which is the M60 R7 class (a name that is not a name).
decisions.pinned_by: markdown/heading-identity, whose `forbidSymbols` half carries the absent-name contract, and F9-PROBE-MD10 for the closing run.

decisions.question: Should a table's BODY rows publish symbols or `contains` edges? RULED: no. A header cell is a column NAME — the identity of the table's structure — and a body cell is DATA.
decisions.measured: 224 `pipe_table_row` sites over 14 of 738 corpus files produce no symbols, and the header-only reading is what the M11 contract named when it fixed the lane's symbol map (`pipe_table -> class`, columns as `contains` children).
decisions.consequence: A table's data is not queryable through this lane. For a documentation graph that is the right trade — the structure is the document's, the values are the reader's — and it is the same ruling toml's spec records for a value being data rather than a node.
decisions.pinned_by: the M12 contract probe's 'contains table -> column', and markdown/payload-lines-evidence for the column edges' line and tier.

decisions.question: Should a raw HTML block publish a symbol? RULED: no, and the cost is attributed to the GRAMMAR rather than the analyzer.
decisions.measured: 579 `html_block` sites over 291 of 738 corpus files. The corpus-errors artifact already names the one construct where the block grammar genuinely fails rather than declining: an indented `<details>` inside a numbered-list item, which recovers with an ERROR node at each list-item boundary, in 2 of 738 files. The remaining 577 sites are regions the grammar models as opaque and the lane correctly declines to invent structure for.
decisions.consequence: A document that is largely HTML (a generated API reference, say) contributes only its markdown skeleton to the graph. Declared, not hidden — and the alternative, fabricating a tree for a region the parser did not resolve, is the 'a guess dressed as a fact' the erlang/html lanes both record as a refusal.
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m12/results/markdown-corpus-errors.json, whose four named grammar limits are the measured half of this ruling.

decisions.question: The block grammar wraps content in `section` nodes. Should a `section` be a symbol, or should the heading hierarchy BE the containment tree? RULED: the heading hierarchy is the tree, and `section` is an internal artifact.
decisions.measured: The M11 contract fixed the symbol map as 'ATX headings -> type with hierarchy', and the M12 ground truth's 59 facts are all heading/table/code containment with no `section` among them.
decisions.consequence: A heading is the document's own structure and a `section` is the grammar's, so publishing the latter would put a node in the graph that no author wrote and no reader navigates by. The heading hierarchy carries the same information with a name the document chose.
decisions.pinned_by: the 59 M12 ground-truth facts and the 31-check M12 contract probe, both of which would gain a `section` row if this ruling were reversed.

decisions.question: Should a link whose destination is only a `#fragment` be published as a `uses` edge to that literal fragment?
decisions.ruling: No — and the fragment must be RESOLVED to the heading it names, or suppressed. A fragment names a heading in the SAME document, written as that heading's GitHub ANCHOR rather than its text. The lane published heading TEXT and had no notion of an anchor, so the two spellings could not meet: `## Install Now!` publishes as `Install Now!` while a link to it says `#install-now`, and nothing in the file is called `install-now`.
decisions.measured: 420 pinned corpus files: 10,174 bare fragments, of which 10,158 resolve to a published heading and 16 name a heading that does not exist. Before, 0 of 10,174 could resolve, by construction.
decisions.rule: Anchors from the heading's display text: lowercase, keep letters/digits/hyphens, spaces and tabs to hyphens, drop the rest; a repeated anchor takes a `-1`, `-2` ordinal. A fragment is percent-decoded (invalid escapes fall back to raw text rather than throwing, so a typo cannot fail a parse) and lowercased before matching. Resolution is DEFERRED to the end of the block walk, because a link may precede its heading. A fragment matching no heading is NOT published — the internal twin of MD-D1 — and the count is disclosed in `metadata.patterns` as `Markdown undefined internal anchors: N` so the measurement survives where the edge does not. Each resolved edge carries the HEADING's line (M59 #825: the line that carries the name the edge is about, and the only choice under which the store's `fileId:name:line` key resolves) with the link's own line kept as `metadata.linkLine`.
decisions.limitation: Non-ASCII LETTERS in a heading diverge from the renderer: GitHub's slugger keeps Unicode letters (`Café` -> `#café`), this lane's slug is ASCII-only, so it would produce `#caf`. The ASCII-only rule is deliberate and MEASURED, not an oversight. The corpus has 24 headings containing non-ASCII characters and all 24 are Unicode PUNCTUATION (the right single quote in `What’s new in the 0.13.0-RC1 technology preview?`), which the renderer also drops, so ASCII-only matches on every one of them; and 0 corpus links target a non-ASCII anchor. Telling a Unicode letter from Unicode punctuation without a pattern IS the whole problem, and this lane's zero-regex property is measured and pinned, so the boundary is declared rather than quietly approximated. Documents affected: 0 as measured, unknown in general — which is the honest form of that sentence.
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m14/fixtures/markdown/internal-anchor-links (six behaviours, incl. forbidRelationships naming the RAW FRAGMENT) + markdown/internal-anchor-unresolved mutant. The oracle implements the same specification INDEPENDENTLY from the tree (script/m14/markdown-oracle.ts mdAnchorSlug/mdDecodeFragment): the specification is external and checkable, so two implementations agreeing is evidence, whereas the shared helper that would have guaranteed agreement is the mistake this lane has now paid for twice.

decisions.question: Should the markdown analyzer emit a `extends` relationship? RULED: no.
decisions.resolution: RULED: markdown emits no `extends` edge, and the construct one needs does not exist. A document declares SECTIONS and a section is CONTAINED in a section, which this lane emits as `contains` (7,603 edges over 322 corpus files, both ends resolving 100.0%); it never inherits from one. Measured: 0 of the 104 node types BOTH pinned grammars produce across a 1,200-file draw is a type declaration or a supertype clause. OVERTURN: the grammar instantiating a type-declaration or superclass node, which `validation/m14/grammar-pins.json` is drift-gated against.
decisions.measured: See script/m14/markdown-ruled.ts (MARKDOWN_RULED) for the instrument's node-type denominator and the overturn condition, and validation/m60/markdown/*.json for the counts.

decisions.question: Should the markdown analyzer emit a `implements` relationship? RULED: no.
decisions.resolution: RULED: markdown emits no `implements` edge. There are no types, so there is nothing to conform to and no endpoint an edge could name. Measured: 0 of the 104 node types either pinned grammar produces is a supertype, conformance or constraint clause. The one corpus construct that binds one document to another BY CONTRACT is a Jekyll `{% include %}`, and that is a binding by FILE, which this lane emits under MD-G3 as a file dependency rather than as a type relationship. OVERTURN: a clause binding a document to a named type, or any grammar node expressing conformance.
decisions.measured: See script/m14/markdown-ruled.ts (MARKDOWN_RULED) for the instrument's node-type denominator and the overturn condition, and validation/m60/markdown/*.json for the counts.

decisions.question: Should the markdown analyzer emit a `exports` relationship? RULED: no.
decisions.resolution: RULED, and this is the type where a grammar alone is NOT enough — json's lane recorded that a grammar cannot see a CONVENTION, and json's own `exports` ruling was overturned by measuring one. So the convention was measured here too, on the document's own reserved positions: front matter and the first H1, 193 occurrences in 193 files on the draw. Every one of the 193 names THE DOCUMENT ITSELF, so the edge would be a self-edge, which is the M60 R7 class. The Jekyll keys that do carry cross-file meaning (`title:`, `permalink:`, `redirect_from:`) live inside `minus_metadata`, which has ZERO named children across 319 nodes in 319 files, so the grammar exposes no key to read. 0 of the 104 node types is an export or manifest node. OVERTURN: a document publishing a name that a DIFFERENT corpus document binds to — measurable by parsing both and looking for the pair, not by reading a spec.
decisions.measured: See script/m14/markdown-ruled.ts (MARKDOWN_RULED) for the instrument's node-type denominator and the overturn condition, and validation/m60/markdown/*.json for the counts.

decisions.question: Should the markdown analyzer emit a `overrides` relationship? RULED: no.
decisions.resolution: RULED: markdown emits no `overrides` edge, and the naive probe for it is wrong on this language in a way worth recording. The bash probe — a second declaration of a name already declared in the file — returns 570 same-parent, same-level, same-text heading redeclarations in 23 of 1,200 files, and 2,453 repeated heading texts at any scope in 50. Those are two SECTIONS sharing a title, not one replacing the other: CommonMark renders both, and the renderer's rule gives each a distinct anchor. Measured: 224 anchors in 61 files are held by more than one heading and 0 of them displace, because the ordinal (`slug`, `slug-1`) exists; `markdown/internal-anchor-links` pins that on `Duplicate` and `Duplicate#2`. So the deciding count is 570 redeclarations and 0 displacements. OVERTURN: a heading becoming unreachable after a later one claims its address, which `markdown/internal-anchor-links` would fail on.
decisions.measured: See script/m14/markdown-ruled.ts (MARKDOWN_RULED) for the instrument's node-type denominator and the overturn condition, and validation/m60/markdown/*.json for the counts.

decisions.question: Should the markdown analyzer emit a `instantiates` relationship? RULED: no.
decisions.resolution: RULED: markdown emits no `instantiates` edge. Measured two ways, because a grammar alone leaves the component case open. 0 of the 104 node types either pinned grammar produces is a construction node. And the component reading is 0 as well: `html_block` holds 1,802 nodes in the draw, 10 contain a `<script>` tag and none carries a `src`, and 0 `html_tag` in the corpus has a capitalised name, so nothing is used as a component. OVERTURN: a capitalised tag inside an `html_block`, or a grammar node expressing a construction.

decisions.question: Should the markdown analyzer emit a `calls` relationship? RULED: no.
decisions.resolution: RULED, with the measured alternative stated because markdown demonstrably CARRIES other languages' programs. 0 of the 104 node types either pinned grammar produces is a call or invocation node. 6,243 fenced code blocks in the 1,200-file draw declare another language in their info string; a call inside one is a fact about that language and an edge emitted from it would name endpoints no markdown file declares, so `bb_impact` would offer to rewrite a caller that does not exist. The delegation route is measured too and is empty: 1,802 `html_block` nodes, 10 carrying a `<script>`, none with a `src`. OVERTURN: a call edge derivable from markdown's own nodes.

counts.falsifier_RUN: Independently of the arbiter, each claimed target's LEAF was tested against the project's own two key spaces (an admitted file whose repo-relative path ends with the leaf, or a published symbol equal to it): **4,107 of 115,365 (3.6%) HIT**. They are coincidences, not refutations — `https://github.com/intellifactory/Bolero/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md` in Bolero hits Bolero's own `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `https://rdatatable.gitlab.io/data.table/` hits the symbol `data.table` — which is exactly why the arbiter's URI refusal is LOAD-BEARING rather than lazy: a leaf-based check (the differential's own `normTarget` identity) would bind 4,107 of these URLs to a local declaration and be wrong every time. NOTHING in the falsifier refutes the claim; it prices the alternative.
counts.the_fixable_half: The lane's `uses` UNRESOLVED column is 9,555: relative path **6,367** · dotted name 2,673 · bare token 487 · fragment 27 · scheme:x 1. Of the 6,367 relative-path targets, **2,464 name a file the project ADMITS** — the CEILING of resolving a repo-relative link to the file it names, which is the language's own rule (a markdown link is relative to the CONTAINING file) and the css-D15 sibling pattern exactly. Priced, not yet measured as a before/after.

They are `src/ast/pool-worker.ts` `extractFallback()` REGEX rows (confidence 0.4-0.6, `metadata.method: "regex"`) produced for files whose parse fell back under load, and the lane's own whole-population census measured the truth on a sequential run: contains 334,773 · uses 270,779 · references 16,857 · imports 105 · **calls 0 · instantiates 0, 0 degraded**. The programme already prints the distinction this needs (`ontology-coverage-gate.ts:945-956`: `DEGRADED (regex fallback, not the analyzer)` and `>>> excluded from EMITTED`), so the fix belongs in the pool worker's degraded path or in the gate's exclusion — NOT in this analyzer, which would have to emit a type its grammar does not have.

counts.ceiling_correction: THE PRICED CEILING WAS 2,464 AND THE FIX REACHED 5,253 — 2.13x it, and the understatement is mine and explained: the ceiling counted a relative target as resolvable only when the ADMITTED FILE LIST held a path matching it exactly (after stripping `./`). decisions.node_type: fenced_code_block (info_string beginning `{`: the MyST brace-directive family)
decisions.closed_as: implemented (part_of, rung R3 — no grammar change)
decisions.measured: The construct census over the WHOLE admitted population (validation/m14/fixtures/markdown/measurements/extended-construct-census.json, admission = git ls-files per repo, .md/.markdown, < 1 MiB, 17,460 files): 72,786 fenced code blocks, of which 317 carry a brace-directive info string — all in the wagtail repository — and of THOSE, 2 are file-inclusion `include` directives (`literalinclude` measured 0 sites): 1 SPLICE (wagtail/docs/advanced_topics/icons.md:109, `{include} ../_static/wagtail_icons_table.txt`, no options) and 1 FRAGMENT-QUOTED (wagtail/docs/reference/ui/client.md:3, `{include} ../../../client/README.md` with `:start-after:`/`:end-before:`). The splice/fragment split is the `part_of` contract's own test: an inclusion with NO fragment option inserts the whole file into this document's scope (a part); an option that quotes a fragment makes the file a quote SOURCE, and the census counts that split 1/1. THE GRAMMAR SHAPE IS MEASURED, not read off a spec: the pinned block grammar models the fence as `fenced_code_block > fenced_code_block_delimiter, info_string, fenced_code_block_delimiter`, with the brace directive as the info string's own text (`{include} path`) and the directive name as its `language` child — the same named nodes the analyzer's code-block arm already reads, which is what makes this rung R3. THE EXECUTION SHAPE IS MEASURED TOO: a single wasm heap aborts (`Aborted()`) after ~8,400 parses (first run lost 9,057 of 17,460 files; a same-process retry recovered 0), so the census runs as fresh-process shards of ~4,365 files (a size measured safe at 4,365/4,365/4,365 parsed in the first run), spawned SEQUENTIALLY — 8 concurrent shards interfere (each parsed only ~700), which is the arm-token rule's own lesson re-learned: one heavy thing at a time.
decisions.rule: part_of is emitted for a fence whose info string begins `{`, whose directive is `include` or `literalinclude`, whose argument is a non-empty path-shaped token, and whose content carries NO fragment option (`:lines:`, `:start-after:`, `:end-before:`, `:start-line:`, `:end-line:`, `:lineno-*`). THE TARGET IS SYMBOL-SHAPED: the included file's module stem (basename minus extension), never the raw path — the cpp lane measured a path target resolving 0 of 4,612 rows — and the path as written is kept on the row as `metadata.partPath`. `metadata.partRole: "library"` is MANDATORY (the vocabulary's own contract, src/ast/types.ts PartOf): this file is the including document and the directive names the part. Confidence 1.0 and evidenceClass `import_based`, the same tier erlang/php/fsharp gave their part_of relabels. The four near misses are EXCLUDED by rule and pinned by the fixture's forbid half: a fence with a LANGUAGE is code (72,469 of 72,786 corpus fences); a fragment-quoted include is counted in `metadata.patterns` (`Markdown fragment-quoted include (not part_of)`) and never published; a markdown link and an image are `uses` edges, not inclusions; a brace directive that is not an inclusion (`{note}` 93, `{contents}` 84, `{eval-rst}` 79, `{code-block}` 20, `{warning}` 15, `{toctree}` 13 in the census) is an admonition/nav node.
decisions.population: 17,460 admitted files (git ls-files per repo, .md/.markdown, < 1 MiB); 72,786 fences; 317 brace-directive fences; 2 inclusion sites; 1 splice site. Corpus-wide the construct is rare — a MyST-ism — and the emission is measured on the whole population, not on a MyST-heavy sample.
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m14/fixtures/markdown/brace-include-part-of (two positive rows pinning `{include}` and `{literalinclude}` splice forms with partPath/partRole/evidenceClass/line; seven forbid rows pinning the language fence, the fragment-quoted include, the raw-path target spelling, the markdown link, the image, the `{note}` admonition and the bare `{include}`) + the census artifact validation/m14/fixtures/markdown/measurements/extended-construct-census.json. FALSIFIER: a brace-inclusion fence in the admitted population that carries NO fragment option and publishes no part_of row — the census's own `splice: 1` site (wagtail/docs/advanced_topics/icons.md:109) is the run falsifier; a gate arm over the whole admitted population reading a part_of row other than 1 falsifies the count.
decisions.why_it_was_open: `part_of` joined the vocabulary 2026-10-18 and this lane had never adjudicated it. The construct was found by measuring which fence info strings the corpus actually carries rather than by reading a spec: the brace-directive family is 0.4% of fences and 100% of it lives in one repository's MyST docs, so a sample short of wagtail would have measured zero and a ruling would have been written from the sample. The ladder was walked: R1 (a different grammar build) unnecessary — the pinned build already carries the directive in named nodes it publishes; R2 (patch) unnecessary — nothing is missing from the grammar; R3 (express on an existing node type) is the rung taken.

relationship_kinds_declared_absent._corrected: `imports` and `references` were listed below as declared-absent until 2026-10-09, and both entries were FALSE by measurement: both are emitted and both fire (see _relationship_kinds_produced_corrected, coverage.implemented, and validation/m14/fixtures/markdown/firing-corpus-census.json). They were stale prose from before MD-G3 (2026-10-03) and MD-D6, left behind when the analyzer changed — which is exactly the failure mode this section's own `note` names. The six that remain are the six grammar-absence exclusions in `coverage`, each re-measured on current bytes with a planted control.
relationship_kinds_declared_absent.exports: a markdown file exports nothing; it is a leaf of the project's file tree.
relationship_kinds_declared_absent.calls: no call syntax exists in CommonMark.
relationship_kinds_declared_absent.extends: no inheritance syntax exists in CommonMark.
relationship_kinds_declared_absent.implements: no interface syntax exists in CommonMark.
relationship_kinds_declared_absent.overrides: no member syntax exists in CommonMark.
relationship_kinds_declared_absent.instantiates: no constructor syntax exists in CommonMark.
relationship_kinds_declared_absent.imports: markdown has no module system. There is nothing to import, and a `uses` edge to a relative path is a LINK, not a dependency — bb_doc's Dependencies section stays empty for a .md file for exactly this reason, which is a real consequence of the ruling and not an oversight.
relationship_kinds_declared_absent.references: the lane declares front-matter keys as a boundary rather than a graph: `title:`, `permalink:`, `redirect_from:` and `weight:` are the cross-file link carriers in a Jekyll site and the block grammar models `minus_metadata` as ONE node with no key/value children, so there is no key to reference from. Declared, with the reason, rather than left silent.

evidence_tiers.contains: structural — a parent/child relation read off the block tree
evidence_tiers.uses: reference_qualified — the destination is a node's own text, and for a reference link the destination the document's own definition declares
evidence_tiers.measured: 11,401/11,401 relationships over the pinned corpus carry a 1-based line_number and an evidenceClass from the closed vocabulary. Before this round it was 0/9,132, and because graph-core's read-time derivation does not list `contains` among its structural types the entire heading hierarchy was rendered to readers as `inferred` — 'a guess, treat as a hint, never as fact' — for edges that cannot be anything else.

closed_gaps.measured: An indented (four-space) code block published NOTHING while the fenced form beside it published a per-site `function`, so a reader could not tell 'this document has no code' from 'this document has code the lane dropped'. CORRECTION TO THE ORIGINAL ESTIMATE, and the correction is the interesting part: the gap recorded '2 sites in 2 of 738 corpus files', measured by a text heuristic for four-space-indented lines — which mostly matches wrapped list-item continuation, not code. Measured with the BLOCK GRAMMAR over 1,138 pinned corpus files (738 scala3 + 400 kubernetes) the figure is 217 nodes, 100x the estimate. All 217 now publish.
closed_gaps.population_note: Most of the 217 are not authored code. They are the wrapped continuation lines of deeply-nested list items, which CommonMark genuinely reads as indented code: `* a bullet` / `    * a nested bullet` / `        the wrapped text`. The grammar is right and the author did not mean a code block. They are published anyway, because the alternative is the asymmetry this closes, and because a consumer that cares can read `nodeType: indented_code_block` and the range and discount them. A population 100x the original estimate is a fact about the ESTIMATE, not about the construct — and the estimate was made with the wrong instrument, which is the generalisable half of this entry.
closed_gaps.rule: One more node type on the block DFS, sharing the fenced path's site identity so the two forms cannot collide: a fence with no info string and an indented block under one heading both publish `code_block`, so the second is `code_block#2`. A block with a language keeps it in its NAME (`code_block.scala`) and therefore has its own base, so the ordinal never reaches it. An indented block publishes NO `language` key at all: the construct has nowhere to declare one, and the fence's `text` default means 'a fence that declared none', which is a different fact. The ORACLE derives the node too — a differential that derived fenced blocks and stopped at indented ones would be asserting that a document with an indented block and one without it have the same truth, and leaving it alone turned the fix into 5 unexplained edges on the kubernetes draw.
closed_gaps.pinned_by: validation/m14/fixtures/markdown/indented-code-block (three properties + a control section where an indented line is a NESTED LIST ITEM and must publish nothing, so the fixture cannot be satisfied by treating any indentation as code) + markdown/indented-code-block-dropped mutant, whose assertion is the symbol COUNT rather than a name for the reason given in its description.
closed_gaps.why_it_was_open: Left open rather than classified silent on purpose. `internal_silent` means 'correctly emits nothing', and for a code block the correct answer is a symbol — the fenced form proves the lane has one. Classifying it silent would have made the count zero and the question closed, which is the 'silent gap' the M14 standing rules call the actual shame.

closed_gaps.measured: The node is declared in the pinned block grammar's node-type list — which is why the union census counts it among the 72 named types — but never instantiated. The bare Pandoc `+++` form parses to a `paragraph`; the MyST `<!--[metadata]>` + `+++` form parses to an `html_block`. Across all 5,501 markdown files in every pinned corpus, 18 carry MyST title-block metadata (docker/api/docs) and the grammar produces ZERO `plus_metadata` nodes for any of them. The gap's own recorded population of '0 sites in 738 corpus files' was true and misleading: it was true of the lane's DECLARED corpus, and the wider measurement found 18 files that look like candidates.
closed_gaps.rule: No analyzer branch. A front-matter branch keyed to this node type would be dead code, because the node never arrives, and the only way to read a `+++` title block is to parse the paragraph's TEXT — which is precisely what this lane's zero-regex, every-fact-AST-derived rule forbids. The asymmetry the gap complained about (the `---` spelling is handled and the `+++` spelling is not) is not the analyzer's to close: the grammar reads one as front matter and the other as prose.
closed_gaps.forward_obligation: If a future grammar instantiates the node, the grammar pin goes red on `typeSetDigest` or `fieldSetDigest` (it is drift-gated on all ten surface keys) and this entry is where the obligation is written down. A pin that detects its own trigger is a real mechanism; a TODO in a spec is not.
closed_gaps.pinned_by: The classification itself (completeness section A: 30 handled / 42 silent / 0 gaps / 6 decisions) plus the grammar pin's surface drift gate, which is the detector. No fixture is written here, and deliberately: a fixture for a node the grammar never produces would assert nothing, which is the same reason the gap was filed as unpinnable in the first place.
